To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a deep learning based method can achieve better restoration performance than existing SR methods, b) traditional sparse coding based methods can be interpreted as a deep convolution network, c) a deep CNN can be optimized jointly, and d) our deep CNN has a very lightweight structure and achieves state of the art performance.
We propose a deep convolutional model for single image super-resolution, which is the first deep learning model for this task.

1) We present a deep learning method, which learns an end-to-end mapping between the low and high resolution images, and 2) We demonstrate that traditional sparse coding-based super resolution methods can be also viewed as a deep learning method.

the following questions:

the following questions: (1) Can we learn a deep CNN to directly map a low resolution image to its high resolution counterpart? (2) Can we learn such a CNN end to end? (3) How to optimize the deep CNN? and (4) What is the relationship between our method and traditional SR methods?

two major issues: (1) the design of an end to end learning based SR method that can be used in practical applications; and (2) the analysis of the relationship between traditional sparse coding based methods and our deep learning based method.
